KISS ceiling: #5783 Prefer-A Bound 6280270826 (Thin Fail-Closed #3265 / writing-bar #3368)

## In plain English

Retiring a shipped brief (active→completed rename, clause restamp, CHANGELOG line) is not product work for some other live story. The write guard still wants an active scope. Completed-folder edits already skip that gate (#4422), and proposed/ planning writes already skip it (#2625), but the retirement transition still touches active/ plus CHANGELOG, so the completed-only exemption does not cover it. Workers then either stop or pin an unrelated active brief. Prefer-A extends the existing lifecycle-exemption family so a narrow retirement/restamp mutation set is admitted without borrowing another story, and the deny text names that path when the set does not qualify. #3631 stays a related provenance/CI keep-out, not this arc.

## Approaches

### Approach A — Extend lifecycle exemption for retirement/restamp (Prefer-A lean)

Add one exemption class beside write-propose-ready / write-completed-ready: when every harvested mutation target is a same-slug active↔completed lifecycle brief path (xbrief/ or legacy vbrief/) and/or CHANGELOG.md, and the brief under move is shipped/orphan-eligible (issue closed or linked PR merged / leftover-complete class), admit without an active scope and without DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE. Mixed product paths stay denied. scope-not-ready copy names this sanctioned path when the mutation looks like retirement but fails the predicate. Reuse #4422/#2625 universal-quantification over harvested targets. Fixture locks the #5888-shaped rename+CHANGELOG path and refuses unrelated-scope borrow.

### Approach B — Mint a standing maintenance scope type

Introduce a durable chore/maintenance brief class whose file_scope is only lifecycle brief folders plus CHANGELOG.md, activate it for retirement PRs, and keep ordinary active-scope gating. Heavier than A: new scope taxonomy, activation chore, and conflict with empty-active / one-scope recovery copy. Risks becoming the path-allowlist #3631 already rejected for CI provenance.

### Approach C — Hand-edit refuse; scope:complete only

Deny all hand retirement; denial names task scope:complete as the sole path. Leaves restamp/CHANGELOG hand edits and cases where scope:complete cannot run (already-completed restamp, multi-brief orphan cleanup mid-PR) without a lawful Write path. Does not meet AC1 for the observed #5888 hand transition.

## Prefer-A package (lean A)

- Mechanism: retirement/restamp lifecycle exemption (same family as #4422 completed + #2625 proposed), not a second DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE pin and not a new standing maintenance story.
- Admit set: all mutation targets ⊆ {same-slug xbrief|vbrief active/completed *.xbrief.json|*.vbrief.json pair for the brief being retired or restamped, CHANGELOG.md}.
- Gate: brief must be leftover/shipped-class eligible; otherwise refuse and name scope:complete / leftover-complete.
- Deny honesty: when no active scope and targets look retirement-shaped but fail the admit set, name the sanctioned exemption (and scope:complete) instead of promote-then-activate / borrow-another-brief.
- AC2: keep story write-fence refuse for an unrelated active brief whose file_scope does not cover the retirement paths (already required; add regression if missing).
- Tests: dispatcher decideHook path covering #5888-shaped active→completed+CHANGELOG allow with inspectScope ready:false; mixed product deny; unrelated-scope fence refuse.
- KISS (#5783): short mechanism limbs only; docs/naming footnotes; remint only for fail-closed association changes.
- Keep-outs: #3631 provenance/CI chore model; inventing DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE for retirement; widening completed exemption to arbitrary active/ edits; soft-green past write fence.

## Reject

- Borrowing an unrelated active brief to clear scope-not-ready for retirement edits.
- Setting DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE (or any pin bypass) as the retirement remedy.
- Path-allowlist-only CI provenance (#3631) as a substitute for this edit-guard admit.
- Treating completed-only #4422 as already closing active→completed+CHANGELOG transitions.

## file_scope lean

- packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts (and adjacent lifecycle-write helpers/tests)
- packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.test.ts
- CHANGELOG.md
- docs pointer only if a one-line recovery path is required for deny copy

Round-1 open critique of Prefer-A draft 6392627499 and Stop 1 6392634211, at dispatch-sha eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940. Input ceiling: 6392657933. Verification: pinned source reads; no fixtures executed.

Inventory before new: [dispatcher.ts:681–704](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L681-L704) already rejects empty/unclassified harvests and quantifies over normalized targets. [The lifecycle allow helper](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L2155-L2207) retains authz, runtime policy and occupancy checks. Completed-only tests already cover mixed product patches. Reuse these; they do not establish a retirement transaction. The existing orphan evaluator also distinguishes shipped from unresolved state.

### F1 — blocks-the-design: the proposed placement does not preserve AC2

Evidence: the lifecycle helper returns before inspectScope and passes scopePath:null into runtimeAuthority. [write-fence.ts:418–424](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts#L418-L424) maps that null to an empty story fence. Thus extending this helper does not “keep story write-fence refuse” for an unrelated selected brief: a qualifying retirement request can return before that brief is inspected. Project policy is still checked, but that is a different fence.

Consequence: A cannot bind with both its proposed placement and its AC2 claim. Specify precedence: either selected-scope writes must satisfy that scope's fence before the new exemption, or a qualified retirement is explicitly independently authorized and AC2 is limited to requests outside that qualification. Lock the chosen behavior with a real selected unrelated scope, not a stub that ignores scopePath.

### F2 — blocks-the-design: a path subset is not a retirement operation

Evidence: allMutationTargetsMatch uses every(target), with no operation direction or pair relationship. A's active↔completed wording admits resurrection, and its subset admits CHANGELOG alone unless a nonempty brief association is separately required. Requiring the pair in every call instead leaves ordinary separate rename/restamp/CHANGELOG calls without that association. [Shell routing](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L2864-L2892) additionally calls inspectMutationGates per classified destination; one synthetic combined-payload fixture cannot prove that path works.

Consequence: bind the sanctioned operation before implementation: active→completed only, or a completed-record correction, with CHANGELOG attached to an identified eligible brief in the admitted operation. Require the whole mutation set to satisfy that association; a same-slug predicate alone is insufficient. Test the actual supported tool payload and reject reverse moves, mismatched slugs, standalone CHANGELOG, and mixed product targets. If separate calls are supported, name how their association survives between calls. #5888 contains two brief renames plus CHANGELOG: explicitly split it into supported operations or support a set of individually verified pairs.

### F3 — blocks-the-design: “orphan-eligible” is broader than shipment proof

Evidence: [orphan-active/evaluate.ts:230–267](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/eaeec287e5ac8d47682c3f10ae48b9a606f79940/packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts#L230-L267) distinguishes confirmed shipment from unresolved lookups. The draft does not identify which pre-write brief supplies the issue/PR association or what happens when that evidence cannot be resolved. Treating an orphan result or newly edited completion metadata as authority could admit an unshipped brief; failing open on lookup errors creates the same hole.

Consequence: require verified shipped status bound to the pre-write brief identity in the effective worktree; unresolved/dropped-reference results must not authorize. Reuse the existing state-resolution machinery, but do not equate a diagnostic failure with eligibility. Test forged/rebound references and unavailable evidence. This is the relevant injection/concurrency boundary: submitted metadata and another tree's same basename must not supply their own authorization.

Road not taken: a standing maintenance scope adds taxonomy without solving association. The strongest case for scope:complete is its explicit operation boundary; it would change my preference if it also supported the required restamp/CHANGELOG flow. A remains the leaner candidate once the three authorization gaps above are closed. Keep #3631's CI provenance model out of this fix.

### Bound remedy

- Define one eligible retirement/correction operation and bind all targets to it.
- Preserve existing guards with explicit selected-scope precedence; fail closed on missing shipment evidence.
- Exercise that operation through decideHook, including the negative cases above, with one supported recovery path.

Naming and recovery-copy polish are footnotes; they do not need a separate mechanism.

## Inventory (pin-read tip)

- isLifecycleFolderWrite (dispatcher.ts:625) admits only proposed|completed + artifact suffix under xbrief/|vbrief/; ^Gctive/ and CHANGELOG.md never match.
- Exempt allow path (2155–2207) runs ^GllMutationTargetsAreProposedLifecycleWrites / …Completed… then ^GllowExemptLifecycleWrite with codes write-propose-ready | write-completed-ready only. Each helper requires every harvested path in one folder class — a mixed active+completed+CHANGELOG set cannot pass either predicate.
- ApplyPatch Move to harvests both source and destination (classify/paths.test.ts #3794), so a same-tool active→completed Move surfaces both ends to universal quantification.
- scope-not-ready recovery (2246–2310) steers SCOPE_NOT_READY_PROMOTE_THEN_ACTIVATE / proposed-filename hint (#2625); no retirement/restamp or scope:complete branch when targets look lifecycle-shaped but fail the admit set.
- Tip has no PreToolUse-safe shipped/orphan eligibility oracle in the lifecycle-exemption family; erify:orphan-active is a separate check task, not a decideHook seam. #2625/#4422 remain pure path predicates.

## Findings

### F1 — Shipped/orphan-eligible gate has no tip PreToolUse oracle

- Class:  locks-the-design

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — Approach A mints the class tip explicitly forbids

**Evidence.** `lifecycle-write.ts:54`: `"Do not Edit/Write completed/. Do not mint a completed/ Write class. "`. Both sentences are locked by `lifecycle-write.test.ts:159-160`. Approach A's admit set ("all mutation targets ⊆ {same-slug … active/completed pair …, CHANGELOG.md}") is a completed/ Write class.

**Failure mode.** Bind A as written and the two surfaces oppose each other on one diff: the PreToolUse gate emits a retire-ready allow for a hand Edit of `xbrief/completed/<slug>.xbrief.json`, and `completed-write-guard` then refuses that land at CI, appending this very string as the remediation (`completed-write-guard.ts:1062`, `:1071`). Green hook, red gate, and the deny text tells the worker to undo what the hook just authorized.

**Disposition.** The lean cannot bind as written. Either the Bound is re-scoped off completed/ Write entirely, or the arc must state that it reverses the keep-out and name `lifecycle-write.ts:44-61` plus `lifecycle-write.test.ts:159-160` as the rewrite sites. ### 2. blocks-the-design — the A-over-C comparison rests on a false premise about tip

**Evidence.** The draft rejects C because it "leaves restamp/CHANGELOG hand edits and cases where scope:complete cannot run (already-completed restamp, multi-brief orphan cleanup mid-PR) without a lawful Write path." Tip says the opposite on both limbs:

**Failure mode.** The one comparison that selected A over C asserts a gap the shipped verb covers. If the verb does cover it, A is new mechanism for an already-solved problem — the thing "inventory existing mechanisms before proposing new ones" exists to prevent.

**Disposition.** The lean cannot bind until the A-vs-C comparison is redone against `scope:complete` as it actually behaves at the dispatch sha. See the steelman for exactly what reproduction would restore A's premise.

### 3. sharpens-framing — P3 is the whole in-inventory defect, and it is one limb

**Disposition.** This is the KISS-#5783-sized Bound: point the `proposedLifecycleExempt` empty-active branch at the existing constant (or a one-line pointer to it). **Evidence.** `isLifecycleFolderWrite` (`dispatcher.ts:626-637`) is a pure lexical predicate: normalize, reject outside-root, `hasArtifactSuffix`, two `startsWith`. No fs, no git, no forge. **Disposition.** Drop the eligibility limb from the write gate. Shipped-state adjudication already lives at `verify:completed-write-guard` — post-hoc, in CI, where it can afford the lookup and where a wrong answer costs a red check rather than a bad allow.

### 5. sharpens-framing — "same-slug" has no referent on the fixture the Bound names

**Evidence.** `allMutationTargetsMatch` (`dispatcher.ts:685-691`) quantifies over one payload's harvested targets. **Evidence.** Decompose the dispatch sha itself, which is this exact shape (`git show --name-status -M eaeec287e…`): `M CHANGELOG.md` plus `R061 xbrief/active/2026-10-23-5807-….xbrief.json → xbrief/completed/2026-10-23-5807-….xbrief.json`. Taking those targets one at a time:

So on a default-policy repo the only genuinely denied target in the canonical shape is `CHANGELOG.md`.

The lens fires: the target changes write authority and runs on a shared-worktree surface.

**Disposition.** Whatever admit binds must route through `allowExemptLifecycleWrite` with a third `code` value, not a parallel branch. ## B1-prime -- blocking: the verb can write *a* CHANGELOG line, but not the one this repo accepts, and the residue lands back on the refused hand edit

**Claim audited.** Limb P1: `scope:complete` "also writes the optional CHANGELOG line into the same verb-owned diff workers stage for the leftover-land PR." Limb P4: regressions "refuse CHANGELOG-only ... hand Writes without inventing a companion admit."

**Evidence -- from the dispatch-sha commit itself.** `eaeec287e` is a leftover-land PR (#5889) and its own message records four passes over that one CHANGELOG line, the last being:

> `fix(changelog): plain-English leftover #5807 Unreleased note` -- "Address SLizard P1 / Greptile P2: describe operator-facing outcome (issue closable; no longer active) **instead of internal bookkeeping**."

The predecessor `860edfc8c` shipped the unrevised shape: `- Fixed - Leftover-complete #4666: active-to-completed xBRIEF after product merge #5883 (lifecycle only). Refs #4666.` That is precisely the string a verb can synthesize from `{brief, --pr, --merge-commit}` -- and precisely the class review bounced one commit later.

The CI bar is not the binding one: `verify:changelog-unreleased` is wired into `check:framework-source` (gate-lists.ts:130-131) and fails only when the Unreleased `- ` set is **unchanged versus merge-base** (CHANGELOG.md:716, #633). A generated bullet clears that. The bar that bites is review prose, and no pin checker enforces it -- so nothing stops the verb emitting a line that passes `deft check` and gets rewritten at review.

**Failure mode.** Worker runs `task scope:complete`; verb writes the bookkeeping bullet; review asks for operator-facing prose; the brief is now in `completed/` so active/ is empty; the rewrite is a **CHANGELOG-only hand Edit at empty-active** -- refused by limb P4 own regression, with recovery copy naming the verb that just wrote the line being rewritten. B1 loop re-enters through the content door instead of the admission door. It is narrower than B1 (review-time, not first-write) but it is the same dead end, and the pin tip is the instance.

**Disposition (smaller than it sounds).** Make the prose operator-supplied, not synthesized: `task scope:complete -- <brief> --pr <n> --changelog-note "<one line>"`. Flag present, the verb writes that text under `[Unreleased]`; flag absent, the verb writes nothing -- which is what "optional CHANGELOG" in lifecycle-write.ts:55 has always meant. Two riders, one line each:

- The bullet must carry `#<issue>`: `[Unreleased]` union-merge dedup is issue-number keyed (resolve-changelog-unreleased.ts:282-290; the #911 "dedup gap on truncated/issue-numberless entries" story is why). Two concurrent leftover PRs otherwise merge to two bullets.
- Name the target heading and insert position (`### Fixed`, top of section). The `- Fixed - ` prefix in `860edfc8c` shows what happens when nobody does.

And the recovery copy must gain the authorship sentence: `LEFTOVER_LAND_PR_REMEDIATION` (lifecycle-write.ts:44-55) names the verb, the git add, and "optional CHANGELOG" in the PR *shape*, but still says nothing about **how the line gets written**. Strongest defence of limb P1 as written: a mechanically generated bullet is *correct*, passes `verify:changelog-unreleased`, and prose quality is a review concern rather than a gate concern -- so verb-writes-default plus human-improves-in-PR is a normal workflow, not a loop. ## C1 -- blocking: the sanctioned prose re-run is not a prose-only operation

**Claim audited.** Limb P1: "Re-running scope:complete with --changelog-note rewrites that issue-keyed Unreleased bullet in place so post-review prose fixes never require a refused empty-active CHANGELOG-only hand Edit."

**What a re-run actually executes.** `restampCompletedBrief` (transition.ts:1276) is the already-completed path. Before any write it runs, in order:

- `discoverDeliveryEvidenceForComplete` (:1281) -- `runGh` / `fetchPrPayload` / `fetchClosingPrRefs`; `!discovered.ok` returns at :1292
- `enforceOnePrUnitForDiscoveredEvidence` (:1295) -- `!ok` returns at :1300
- `evaluateDeliveryGate` (:1302) -- `!gate.ok` returns at :1324

and then, unconditionally: `planObj.updated = nowIso` (:1327), `stampExistingEnvelopes(data, nowIso)` (:1329), `stampCompletionMetadata(..., nowIso)` (:1330), `stampLifecycleWrite(planObj, "complete", nowIso)` (:1333), `atomicWriteBrief` (:1335), plus a `writeSessionCompletedMarker` whose failure is a hard return (:1351-1358).

**Two consequences, both against the limb own guarantee.**

1. **The escape hatch is network- and gate-conditional.** A one-line prose fix now rides three delivery gates and a `gh` round trip. Offline, or with evidence re-discovery drifting between run 1 and run 2 (closing-PR set changed, one-PR-unit now trips), the verb returns before writing anything. The CHANGELOG line is not rewritten, the brief is in `completed/`, active is empty, and the only remaining move is the hand Edit limb P4 refuses. Same dead end, reached through the gate door instead of the admission door. "Never require" is the phrase that fails.

2. **The hatch is not minimal.** A note-only re-run restamps the completed brief with fresh timestamps on every invocation. A reviewer asking for one line of prose gets a second `completed/` artifact diff on an already-reviewed leftover-land PR -- the exact artifact class the Greptile partition in `LEFTOVER_LAND_PR_REMEDIATION` (lifecycle-write.ts:44-55) is most sensitive about.

**Disposition (one limb sentence).** Say that `--changelog-note` on an **already-completed** brief with no new delivery selectors takes a prose-only path: rewrite the issue-keyed bullet, skip delivery re-discovery and the re-stamp. P4 then locks it as -- note-only re-run writes the revised bullet and leaves the completed brief byte-identical, with the `runGh` / `runGit` seams unused. That keeps the re-run hermetic, which is what makes it a recovery path rather than a second chance to fail.

## S1 -- sharpening: "issue-number keying" names no derivation, and the pin brief is a four-issue cohort

Limb P1 requires the bullet to be issue-number keyed and the re-run to find it again. The pin own leftover brief is the counterexample: `xbrief/completed/2026-10-23-5807-ovpr-hooks-dual-pretooluse-brief-gates-disable-hatch.xbrief.json` carries four `x-xbrief/github-issue` references -- #5807, #5808, #5809, #5869 -- while the bullet it shipped keyed on #5807 alone (CHANGELOG.md:22, `Refs #5807`). Two cases are unspecified:

- **Which number keys a cohort brief?** Keying on all of them is actively harmful: `unionMerge` treats issue-number overlap as any-match (resolve-changelog-unreleased.ts:233-239), so a four-number bullet would dedup away an unrelated branch #5808 or #5869 entry.
- **What keys a brief with no github-issue reference?** `xbrief/completed/2026-04-14-bdd-vbrief-context.xbrief.json` has none. With no key `issueNumbers` returns empty (:145) and `unionMerge` falls back to a truncated lowercased `contentPrefix` (:173-181), under which a *reworded* note is simply a different entry. In-place rewrite degenerates to append, and the duplicate-bullet-on-re-run hazard my PA-2 footnote flagged returns through the keyless door.

A derivation already exists to lean on rather than mint: delivery-evidence.ts:291 resolves the expected repository and issue from the plan `x-xbrief/github-issue` reference, and fails loudly when there is none (:544). Name it, and say what the verb does when it yields nothing -- refuse, or write keyless and accept append-not-rewrite.

## S2 -- sharpening: both copy sites need an all-targets quantifier, and one needs a siting note

The retirement-shape predicate has to quantify over the whole payload at both sites.

- **Empty-active site.** `mutationTargets` is already in hand at dispatcher.ts:2241 and `allMutationTargetsAreCompletedLifecycleWrites` (:700) is the house all-targets pattern, so the predicate is in-inventory. But the surrounding branch reads single-target `relTarget` (the proposed-hint arm, :2272-2279). Say all-targets explicitly, or a payload of `CHANGELOG.md` + `src/foo.ts` picks up leftover-land copy on a product edit -- the leak the Bound own Reject bullet aims at.
- **Write-fence site.** dispatcher.ts:1332 loops `normalized.paths` and returns on the **first** disallowed target (:1338-1347). A mixed payload that happens to hit `CHANGELOG.md` first would emit leftover-land copy for what is product work. The shape test must run over `normalized.paths` as a set before the loop, not on the failing target.
- **Siting.** The message at that return is `verdict.reason` from `evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite` -- a policy-library string, not a dispatcher constant. The lean covers dispatcher.ts, so append at the call site; say so, or limb P2 reads as a request to edit the policy library.

## S3 -- sharpening: the lean omits the file that makes the flag discoverable

Limbs P2 and P3 are discoverability limbs: they only work if a worker who reads the deny can then find the flag. `scope:complete --help` does **not** render the usage string in `scope/main.ts:93-102`. main.ts:358-361 hands `--help` to `interceptHelp("scope_lifecycle", argv)`, and `renderVerbHelp` (triage/help/index.ts:93) renders `entry.usage` and `entry.flags` out of `packages/core/src/triage/help/registry-data.ts` -- the `task scope:complete` entry at :867, usage at :873, flags at :878.

That file is not in the file_scope lean. #3721 already locks this surface (`literal-acceptance/inline-prose-mention.test.ts:314-319` asserts the registry help names `--merge-commit` and `--pr N`), so shipping the flag without a registry entry is both a discoverability hole and a near-miss on a live content contract. Add `packages/core/src/triage/help/registry-data.ts` to the lean; the matching assertion belongs beside the #3721 one.

## Footnotes (no remint; KISS #5783 / #3368)

- **"Optional" is not optional here.** `verify:changelog-unreleased` is `changelog-check --against-merge-base` (tasks/verify.yml:260-266), wired into `check:framework-source` (gate-lists.ts:131), and `runChangelogCheck` has no diff-shape carve-out (task-surface/index.ts:134-166) -- it fails when the Unreleased set is unchanged versus merge-base. On this repo framework-source lane a leftover-land PR with the flag absent is red. "Flag absent writes no CHANGELOG line" is a correct verb contract; the word *optional* is consumer-repo-true and framework-source-false. One clause in the recovery copy, not a limb.
- **The in-place rewrite guarantee is branch-local.** resolve-changelog-unreleased.ts:224-243 drops branch entries whose issue numbers overlap the HEAD side, silently -- warnings are emitted only for orphan headers (:191-196). Once the v1 bullet is on the default branch, a *conflicting* same-issue rewrite loses to HEAD and CI stays green. Pre-merge rewrites are safe; say the guarantee is branch-local rather than unqualified.
- **Duplicate subsection headings are a live state.** The pin `[Unreleased]` carries two `### Changed` headings (CHANGELOG.md:10 and :16). A "named Fixed-section insert" needs a first-match-or-all-matches rule for both the insert and the in-place lookup, plus a stated behaviour when `### Fixed` or `[Unreleased]` is absent -- consumer repos run this verb too.
- **Who names the section.** Three pin `### Fixed` bullets open `- Fixed - ` (CHANGELOG.md:22-24). With operator-authored notes the verb must not concatenate a section word; `860edfc8c` is what happens when writer and author both think they own it.
- **Two prefixes, one flag.** `HISTORICAL_SHIP_CLOSEOUT_HINT` (hooks/scope.ts:77-81) says `deft scope:complete -- <brief> --merge-commit <sha> --pr <n>`; `LEFTOVER_LAND_PR_REMEDIATION` says `task scope:complete`. The Bound already footnotes the split -- extend it to say whether the multiple-eligible audience also learns `--changelog-note`.
- **#3631 keep-out holds.** Nothing above reaches the CI provenance chore model.
- **Decision-code naming and the shell `git mv` residual** stay footnotes under KISS #5783. No harvest.

## Steelman / road not taken

Strongest defence of C1 as written: `scope:complete` is one verb, and giving it a second gate-skipping personality for note-only re-runs is exactly the mode-splitting KISS #5783 rejects -- better one path that always proves delivery than two that can disagree about whether it was proved. That reading is fair, and it is why the disposition above is a condition on inputs the verb already parses (already-completed source folder, no new delivery selectors) rather than a new verb or a `--no-gate` flag. The delivery facts were proved on run 1 and stamped into the brief by `stampDeliveryProvenance` (transition.ts:1320-1326); re-proving them from the network on a prose edit is not a stronger guarantee, only a flakier one.

What would flip C1: a pin-level showing that `restampCompletedBrief` already short-circuits when the brief carries stamped delivery provenance and no new selectors are passed. I do not find one -- :1281 runs discovery unconditionally and :1327-1333 restamp unconditionally.

Recut-2’s --changelog-note re-run still walked full delivery rediscovery and restamped the completed brief, so a prose-only fix could fail offline or dirty an already-reviewed leftover-land PR and strand the worker on a refused hand Edit. Recut-3 makes already-completed note-only re-runs prose-only: rewrite the issue-keyed Unreleased bullet, skip delivery rediscovery and brief restamp. Issue keying uses the existing github-issue delivery resolver and refuses when none. Help registry lists --changelog-note.

## Bound remedy

- relieves: P3 — Empty-active recovery appends LEFTOVER_LAND_PR_REMEDIATION only when every harvested target is retirement-shaped (CHANGELOG.md and/or xbrief|vbrief active/** or completed/**); otherwise keep promote-then-activate / proposed-planning guidance.
- relieves: P2 — Leftover-land recovery and leftover-shaped outside-file_scope denies name task scope:complete --changelog-note and must not steer borrow-another-brief or DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE.
- relieves: P1 — task scope:complete owns active→completed and already-completed restamp; optional CHANGELOG writes only when --changelog-note supplies operator prose under [Unreleased] Fixed (first-match), issue-keyed via the existing x-xbrief/github-issue delivery resolver, refusing when that resolver yields no issue number.
- relieves: P1 — On an already-completed brief with --changelog-note and no new delivery selectors, take a prose-only path that rewrites the issue-keyed Unreleased bullet and leaves the completed brief bytes unchanged without delivery rediscovery or restamp.
- relieves: P1 — Do not mint a PreToolUse completed/ Write class and do not widen allowExemptLifecycleWrite for CHANGELOG companions or active/ hand edits.
- relieves: P4 — Regressions cover retirement-shaped all-targets recovery append-vs-keep, --changelog-note present/absent, prose-only already-completed note rewrite with unused gh seams and byte-identical brief, help-registry discoverability, refuse CHANGELOG-only hand Writes, and unrelated-brief write-fence refuse for nonqualifying hand Writes.

## Authorization precedence

Leftover-land close-out is independently authorized through the scope:complete CLI verb. Qualifying leftover-land hand Writes are not independently admitted. AC2 / unrelated-brief write-fence claims apply only to nonqualifying hand Write/Edit/ApplyPatch requests that still traverse inspectScope.

## Reject

- Recut-2 re-run that re-proves delivery and restamps completed/ for a note-only prose fix.
- PreToolUse CHANGELOG companion admit; wholesale replacement of non-retirement empty-active copy; DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE; #3631 absorb.

Recut-3 answers the keyless one ("refusing when that resolver yields no issue number") and leaves the cohort one unanswered - and by naming `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef` it answers that half by accident, as first-ref-wins. That half, plus two joins downstream of it, is B1.

## B1 - blocking: "the issue-keyed Unreleased bullet" has no unique referent at any of its three joins

Limb P1: "rewrites the issue-keyed Unreleased bullet". Getting from an operator's note to one bullet crosses three joins. The Bound specifies a refusal at the first, and only for the empty case; the other two are unspecified. All three fail **open** - onto an already-reviewed leftover-land PR.

### Join 1 - which issue

`resolvePlanGithubIssueRef` (delivery-evidence.ts:335-356) returns the **first** reference whose URI parses, and its `fromType` test is never load-bearing: `if (!fromType && parsed === null) continue; if (parsed !== null) return parsed;` - any issue-shaped URI wins regardless of ref type.

Corpus at pin, over 1866 `xbrief/completed/*.xbrief.json`: **187** carry more than one distinct typed `x-xbrief/github-issue` number; **4** resolve a winner out of an `x-xbrief/refs` link rather than the origin. The pin's own leftover brief is in the first class (#5807 / #5808 / #5809 / #5869 - the resolver picks #5807 by listing order, not by decision).

### Join 2 - which bullet

Grant one issue: issue to bullet is still 1-to-many in the pin's own `[Unreleased]`. `#5879` keys **two** bullets, CHANGELOG.md:26 and :27, **both inside the single `### Fixed`** at :20. `#5807` keys four - :12 under `### Changed`, and :22 / :23 / :30 under `### Fixed`. "First-match Fixed heading" narrows the heading, not the bullet.

Concretely: a note-only re-run intended for the leftover bullet (:22, "record #5807 complete") silently rewrites the product bullet (:23, the Grok wrapper fix) if first-match wins. That is the exact artifact harm the prose-only path was minted to avoid, reached from the other end.

### Join 3 - what counts as keyed

The repo's only issue-key extractor, `extractIssueNumbers` (platform/linear-scan.ts:146-170), matches the parenthesised `(#N)` form only. Pin house style is bare `Refs #N.` Of 16 `[Unreleased]` bullets, **2** are keyed - :26 `(#4714)` and :31 `(#5796)` - and **14** are not, including every Fixed leftover bullet the path exists to rewrite (:22-:25) and the slash-cohort `(#5807/#5808/#5809/#5869, ...)` at :12, where the digits are not followed by `)`.

So the limb has two candidate groundings and they disagree on the live file:

- Reuse the extractor: the lookup matches nothing on 14 of 16 bullets, `unionMerge` falls through to the truncated `contentPrefix` (resolve-changelog-unreleased.ts:173-181), and a *reworded* note is a different entry - in-place rewrite degenerates to append. Duplicate bullet: PA-2's hazard through a new door.
- Hand-roll a bare-`#N` matcher: the repo then carries two incompatible notions of "issue-keyed", and the other one is still what decides conflict resolution.

**Disposition (one limb plus one regression clause).** Make the key a refusal condition rather than a search hint: the prose-only path refuses unless the resolver yields exactly one issue number **and** that number selects exactly one bullet under the first-match `### Fixed`, printing the candidates on refusal; and say which grammar counts as keyed. P4 then locks cohort-brief refuse, two-candidate-bullet refuse, and bare-`Refs #N` keying. Refusing an ambiguous rewrite is cheap - the operator re-runs with the bullet named. Writing the wrong bullet is not.

## B2 - blocking: the P3 mis-steer survives at the commit site the sanctioned sequence actually reaches

`SCOPE_NOT_READY_PROMOTE_THEN_ACTIVATE` has four emission sites at pin: dispatcher.ts:2256 (spawn), :2288 (empty-active Write recovery), :2293 (shared `else`), and :4851. The Bound's P3 limb is sited on the recovery pair. The fourth - the prospective scope-cover gate on Shell `git commit` (#5656 limb 3, declared at :345) - is untouched.

Leftover-land lands there because `isLifecycleOrInstallerRelPath` (:4808-4816) is `xbrief/` plus `vbrief/` plus managed hook deposits: **`CHANGELOG.md` is not lifecycle.** So the canonical leftover-land staged set {`xbrief/completed/<brief>.xbrief.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`} does **not** take the "Lifecycle/installer-only staged set" ok at :4834; `productStaged` is `["CHANGELOG.md"]`, and with the active set empty `!scope.ready` denies at :4846 with the interpolated `SCOPE_NOT_READY_PROMOTE_THEN_ACTIVATE` recovery.

That is P3 verbatim - scope-not-ready recovery steering promote-then-activate instead of naming leftover land - and it fires on the step `LEFTOVER_LAND_PR_REMEDIATION` itself prescribes: "git add of that verb's already-written diff, then open the leftover-land lifecycle PR". The association miss is the blocking part, not the deny.

**Disposition.** Extend the P3 limb to :4846: when the staged set is lifecycle plus `CHANGELOG.md` only and the active set is empty, name leftover land and `task scope:complete --changelog-note` rather than promote-then-activate. Strongest defence of B1 as written: first-match is the ordinary convention for this kind of rewrite, the operator can read the diff before committing, and piling three refusal conditions onto a one-line prose hatch is exactly the ceremony KISS #5783 rejects. ### B1 - blocks-the-design: commit admission needs a content association, not only the verb's path shapes

At the pin, dispatcher.ts:4741-4762 lists staged paths and passes them to evaluateProspectiveScopeCover. Its input at :4775-4787 carries paths, scope/fence readers and environment; :4822-4833 normalizes and classifies paths. This route has no staged-blob association check. The existing lifecycleWrite stamp (scope/lifecycle-write.ts:25-35, :86-100) records action/time/migration and is replaced on stamping; it does not certify CHANGELOG content. The proposed entry tag supplies owner identity, but its presence alone does not certify the rest of the staged file.

Counterexample: start with unrelated edits to a product bullet or released section in CHANGELOG.md. Run the sanctioned prose-only correction, then stage CHANGELOG.md. This singleton has the same path shape and owned tag as the clean correction. A path-shaped admit accepts both. Refusing hand Writes does not establish that pre-existing or externally made staged changes came from the verb.

Disposition: require the existing commit-admission limb to check the staged CHANGELOG delta against the selected verb-owned tagged entry, failing closed on unrelated hunks or missing/ambiguous association. Apply it to both admitted shapes and add the same-path contamination negative control beside the mixed-product control. Reuse the existing tag carrier and commit gate; no general provenance subsystem is requested. An unstaged worktree tag must not authorize a different index blob. This changes the Bound's fail-closed association and P4 coverage, hence harvest-changed: true.

- Absent because no close-out bullet exists yet (only the product bullet carries the issue) — append is right, and the Recut says so.
- Absent because the close-out bullet exists but predates the tag — append duplicates it.

At pin the second case is the entire population. `LifecycleWriteStamp` is `{ action, writtenAt, migration? }` (scope/lifecycle-write.ts:26-36); no field on it can name a bullet. Across all **1866** `xbrief/completed/*.xbrief.json`, exactly **one** brief carries any `lifecycleWrite` key outside `{action, writtenAt, migration}` — `2026-09-30-5171-...`, with legacy `mergeCommit`/`pr` — and **zero** carry anything bullet-shaped. The prose-only path is defined as firing "on an already-completed brief" — every already-completed brief at pin is untagged. metadata.issueBody:
## What happens
Retiring a shipped xBRIEF (moving it from active to completed, restamping clause evidence or dispositions, adding a CHANGELOG line) isn't implementation work for any one active story. Directive's edit guard still requires an active scope before edits are allowed. With nothing proper to select, a worker can only stop or point the scope at an unrelated active brief to get past the guard. Pointing it elsewhere defeats the guard and records the work against the wrong story.

## Expected
- There's a sanctioned scope for brief maintenance: retiring, restamping or deferring clauses on briefs whose issue already shipped. It's limited to `vbrief/` paths and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Or the guard admits edits bound to the brief being retired, even though that brief is leaving the active set.
- When no scope fits, the guard's refusal names the supported path, so a worker stops and reports instead of borrowing another story's scope.

## Acceptance
1. A brief-retirement change (active to completed, plus a clause restamp and a CHANGELOG line) can be made under a sanctioned scope without selecting an unrelated active brief.
2. Selecting an unrelated brief's scope for edits outside its files is refused or flagged.
3. A test covers the retirement path through the guard.

## Related
- #3631 (framework chore changes need a provenance model, not a path allowlist)
- #5888 (brief-retirement PR where this was hit)
